Rashi on Ketubot 57b:10:1.english: She is given thirty days - From the time of betrothal.

Rashi on Ketubot 57b:11:1.english: Lest they pour her a cup - of terumah.

Rashi on Ketubot 57b:11:2.english: We read [the text as]: “in her father’s house.”

Rashi on Ketubot 57b:12:1.hebrew: דוכתא מייחד לה - מאחר שהוא זן אותה תמיד, מוציאה מבית אביה ומייחד לה מקום, שלא תפסיד מזונותיו לחלקם לקרוביה:
Rashi on Ketubot 57b:12:1.english: He designates a place for her - Since he feeds her regularly, he removes her from her father's house and designates a place for her, so that she does not waste his provisions [by] distributing them to her relatives.

Rashi on Ketubot 57b:13:1.english: A gleaner - Whom [the Israelite] hires to gather his produce.

Rashi on Ketubot 57b:13:2.english: A gleaner [who is] a priest - A gleaner who is a priest and is hired by an Israelite.

Rashi on Ketubot 57b:14:1.hebrew: משום סימפון - הוא דאמר ארוסה לא תאכל תרומה עד שיגיע זמן שחייב במזונותיה. ולשון סימפון הוא ביטול, כגון שובר המבטל שטר קרוי סימפון, ומום באשה או בבהמה שמבטל המקח קרוי סימפון. והכא גזור בה, שמא ימצא בה מום, ונמצאו קידושי טעות ובטלים, ונמצא שאכלה זרה בתרומה:
Rashi on Ketubot 57b:14:1.english: Due to simfon - This is [the reason] why it says a betrothed woman may not eat terumah until the time arrives that he is obligated in her sustenance. The term simfon means cancellation; for example, a receipt that cancels a promissory note is called a simfon, and a blemish in a woman or in an animal that voids a transaction is called a simfon. And here they decreed regarding her, lest a blemish be found in her, and it would turn out to be a mistaken betrothal and void, and it would turn out that a non-priestess ate terumah.

Rashi on Ketubot 57b:15:1.hebrew: אי הכי נכנסה לחופה ולא נבעלה - קס"ד שעדיין אינו מכיר במומין שבה, ואמאי תני מתני' אפילו למשנה אחרונה עד שתכנס לחופה, וכ"ש דקשיא משהגיע זמן דמשנה ראשונה:
Rashi on Ketubot 57b:15:1.english: If so, [a woman who] entered the wedding canopy and has not engaged in intercourse - [The Gemara] initially assumed that he still does not recognize the blemishes in her, and [if so,] why does the Mishnah teach, even according to the later Mishnah, "until she enters the wedding canopy"? And all the more so is it difficult [regarding the ruling] "once the time has arrived" of the earlier Mishnah.

Rashi on Ketubot 57b:15:2.english: He examines her - Through his female relatives.

Rashi on Ketubot 57b:16:1.english: There is no abrogation with regard to slaves - Defects do not nullify a sale.

Rashi on Ketubot 57b:1:1.english: A woman may not eat, etc. - The reason is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Ketubot 57b:4:1.hebrew: ואימא - מאי ימים? חודש, ועשור — עשרה ימים:
Rashi on Ketubot 57b:4:1.english: And let us say - what [is meant by] "days"? A month; and "ten" [means] ten days.

Rashi on Ketubot 57b:5:1.english: May delay - from marrying until she reaches majority.

Rashi on Ketubot 57b:5:2.hebrew: מימרדא ונפקא - תמרוד בבעלה שלא תוכל לסבול, ותצא ותבא אלי עד שתגדל, ונמצאתי צריך לתכשיטין אחרים:
Rashi on Ketubot 57b:5:2.english: She will rebel and leave - She will rebel against her husband, for she will not be able to bear [it], and she will leave and come to me until she grows up, and I will find myself needing other adornments.

Rashi on Ketubot 57b:6:1.english: To marry her while she is a minor - For it is a burden for her.

Rashi on Ketubot 57b:6:2.hebrew: אבל פוסקין כו' - ודוקא בלא קידושין, אבל קידושין בקטנות לא, עד שתגדל ותאמר: בפלוני אני רוצה:
Rashi on Ketubot 57b:6:2.english: But one may finalize, etc. - And specifically without betrothal; however, betrothal during [her] minority [is] not [permitted], until she grows up and says, "I want so-and-so."

Rashi on Ketubot 57b:7:1.hebrew: נותנין לה שלשים יום כאלמנה - משעת אירוסין, שכיון שבגרה היא מכינה תכשיטין קודם בגרות, שאינה רוצה לשהות עוד:
Rashi on Ketubot 57b:7:1.english: They give her thirty days, like a widow - From the time of betrothal, for since she has reached majority, she prepares [her] adornments before [reaching] majority, because she does not wish to delay any longer.

Rashi on Ketubot 57b:7:2.english: Like one who has been asked - As if he asked her to prepare herself for marriage.

Rashi on Ketubot 57b:7:3.english: Of a virgin - [She is given] twelve months from the time of betrothal.

Rashi on Ketubot 57b:8:1.hebrew: יפר - נדריה בלא שותפות דאב. שמעינן מיניה דבוגרת נמי אינו חייב במזונותיה עד שתשהה י"ב חודש:
Rashi on Ketubot 57b:8:1.english: He may nullify - her vows without the partnership of [her] father. We learn from this that [for] a grown woman as well, he is not obligated in her sustenance until she waits twelve months.

Rashi on Ketubot 57b:8:2.hebrew: וששהתה - והכי קאמר: בוגרת לסוף שלשים, והנערה ששהתה שנים עשר חודש:
Rashi on Ketubot 57b:8:2.english: Or [one] who waited - And this is what it means: a grown woman [bogeret] at the end of thirty [days], or a young woman [na'arah] who waited twelve months.

Rashi on Ketubot 57b:9:1.hebrew: בעל נמי יהבו ליה רבנן זימנא - כדתנן במתני', לפרנס עצמו בצרכי חופה:
Rashi on Ketubot 57b:9:1.english: The husband too, the Rabbis gave him time - As we learned in the Mishnah, to provide himself with the needs of the wedding.

Rashi on Ketubot 57b:9:2.hebrew: ולארוסה שלשים יום - ויש ארוסה שאין נותנים לה אלא שלשים יום, ולקמן מפרש לה:
Rashi on Ketubot 57b:9:2.english: And to a betrothed woman, thirty days - And there is a betrothed woman to whom they give only thirty days, and below [the Gemara] explains it.

Tosafot on Ketubot 57b:13:1.hebrew: לקיט כהן כו' - מעשיר לא פריך, דלא שכיח שיאכל בבית ישראל, וגם אין רגילין להוליך תרומה עמהם; אבל לקוטות רגילין להשתכר עם ישראל, ופעמים מתפרנסים משל עצמם:
Tosafot on Ketubot 57b:13:1.english: "A gleaner [who is] a priest, etc." - [The Gemara] does not ask [this] regarding a wealthy [priest], for it is uncommon for him to eat in an Israelite's house, and furthermore, [wealthy priests] are not accustomed to bringing terumah with them; however, gleaners are accustomed to being hired by an Israelite, and at times they sustain themselves from their own [food].

Tosafot on Ketubot 57b:13:2.hebrew: השתא מדידהו ספו ליה כו' - ולקיט ישראל בבית כה לא חיישינן כלל, דדוקא מלקיט כהן בבית ישראל הוא דפריך, לפי שדרך האכסנאי להשקות לבני הבית כדי למצוא חן בעיניהם, וכשהוא מושיט להם אינו מדקדק מה הוא נותן; אבל ללקיט ישראל בבית כהן, כשפרנסתו עליו, בשעת אכילה מדקדק היטב מה הוא נותן לו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 57b:13:2.english: "Now, they feed him from theirs," etc. - And [as for] an Israelite gleaner in the house of a priest, we are not concerned at all [that he might be fed teruma], for it is specifically regarding a priest gleaner in the house of an Israelite that [the Gemara] raises the objection — because it is the custom of a guest to give drink to the members of the household in order to find favor in their eyes, and when he hands [it] to them he is not careful about what he gives; whereas for an Israelite gleaner in the house of a priest, since his sustenance is [incumbent] upon him, at the time of eating he is very careful about what he gives him.

Tosafot on Ketubot 57b:4:1.hebrew: ואין דנין ימים סתם מימים שנאמר בהם חדש - והא דכתיב "ובכתה את אביה ואת אמה ירח ימים", ודרשינן בשילהי החולץ (יבמות דף מח:): ירח — שלשים, ימים — שלשים, ולא אמר התם "ימים" שנים עשר חודש — משום דכתיב אצל ירח:
Tosafot on Ketubot 57b:4:1.english: And one does not derive [the meaning of] an unspecified [use of the term] "days" from "days" about which "month" is stated - And [regarding] that which is written: "and she shall bewail her father and her mother a month of days" (Deuteronomy 21:13), and we expound at the end of [chapter] HaCholetz (Yevamot 48b): "a month" — thirty [days], "days" — thirty [days], and it does not say there [that] "days" [means] twelve months — [that is] because it is written next to "month".

Tosafot on Ketubot 57b:5:1.hebrew: אי איהי ניחא לה, אביה מאי נפקא ליה מינה - משמע: כיון דלא נפקא ליה מינה, הוי מרידה ופוחתין מכתובתה. ותימה: דאטו משום דאין האב רוצה, נקנוס הקטנה בכתובתה? היא מה פשעה? וי"ל: דהוה לן למימר יגרשנה בלא כתובה, שהרי כתובתה לאב:
Tosafot on Ketubot 57b:5:1.english: If it is agreeable to her, what difference does it make to her father - This implies that since it makes no difference to him, it is [considered] rebellion and we deduct from her ketubah. And this is astonishing: is it really [the case] that because the father does not want [the marriage], we should penalize the minor girl in her ketubah? What wrong did she do? And one can answer that we should say he may divorce her without a ketubah, for her ketubah belongs to the father.

Tosafot on Ketubot 57b:7:1.hebrew: בגרה יום אחד ונתקדשה כו' - וא"ת: ומתני' דקתני דמשתבעה נותנין לה י"ב חודש, היכי משכחת לה, כיון דאין נותנין לעולם אלא ל' יום בבגרות — דמסתמא איירי בנתקדשה כשהיא נערה, כמו שדרך בני אדם, דאסור לקדש את בתו קטנה, ואין פוסקין נמי על הקטנה להשיאה? וי"ל, דדוקא בבגרה ואח"כ נתקדשה קאמר רב הונא דאין לה אלא ל' יום, אבל נתקדשה קודם בגרות — יש לה י"ב חודש משעת תביעה. וטעמא דכשבגרה קודם שנתקדשה אין לה י"ב חודש: דמסתמא הכינה כל תכשיטיה, שאם ימצא לה בעל יהא הכל מוכן; אבל נתקדשה קודם בגרות — אינה מקפדת, שכבר היא מקודשת:
Tosafot on Ketubot 57b:7:1.english: "She has reached her majority, one day, and she is betrothed, etc." - And if you ask: As for the Mishnah that teaches that once [her husband] claims her, she is given twelve months — how can such a case be found, since [a woman] is never given more than thirty days in adulthood — for [the Mishnah] presumably speaks of where she was betrothed when she was a na'arah, as is the way of people, since it is forbidden to betroth one's minor daughter, and one also does not arrange for a minor to marry her off? One can say [in answer] that specifically where she reached majority and afterward was betrothed did Rav Huna state that she has only thirty days, whereas if she was betrothed before majority, she has twelve months from the time of the claim. And the reason that when she reached majority before she was betrothed she does not have twelve months [is] that she presumably prepared all her adornments, so that if a husband should be found for her, everything would be ready; whereas if she was betrothed before majority, she is not particular [to prepare them in advance], since she is already betrothed.

Tosafot on Ketubot 57b:7:2.hebrew: מאי לאו כתבועה דבתולה - ולא מצי לשנויי: אין, כתבועה דבתולה, ובשקידשה ואח"כ בגרה, דפשיטא ליה דאז לא הוי בגר כתבועה. ור"ת מפרש, דסתם האי לישנא דבגרה משמע שנתקדשה בבגר ולא קודם:
Tosafot on Ketubot 57b:7:2.english: What, is it not like a virgin who has been asked - And [the Gemara] could not answer: Yes, [it means] like a virgin who has been asked, and [it refers to a case] where he betrothed her and afterward she reached majority — because it is obvious to [the Gemara] that in that case, reaching majority is not [considered] like being asked. And Rabbeinu Tam explains that this phrasing "she reached majority," without further specification, implies that she was betrothed during [her] majority and not before.

Tosafot on Ketubot 57b:9:1.hebrew: תיובתא דרב הונא תיובתא - תימה, דהכא קאי בתיובתא, ובפ' נערה המאורסה (נדרים דף ע:) אתיא סוגיא סתמא דהש"ס כוותיה, דקאמר אמילתיה דרבי אליעזר [ההיא דבוגרת ששהתה י"ב חודש] דמייתי לעיל: "בוגרת בל' יום סגי, אימא: בוגרת וששהתה" — והיינו כרב הונא. ונראה לפרש דה"ק: "בוגרת בל' יום סגי" — והיכי קתני במתני' "בוגרת ששהתה שנים עשר חודש", דמשמע דבוגרת לא סגי לה בשום ענין בלא שנים עשר חודש? והלא בל' יום סגי, כגון שקידשה לאחר ששהתה י"ב חודש בבגרות! ומשני: תני "בוגרת, וששהתה". והשתא קתני סתם בוגרת בהדי נערה ששהתה שנים עשר חודש, ובהדי אלמנה ששהתה שלשים יום, משום דיש בוגרת שדינה כנערה בשנים עשר חודש, כגון בגרה יום אחד ונתקדשה, ויש בוגרת שדינה כאלמנה, כגון עמדה י"ב חודש בבגרותה ונתקדשה; והשתא אתיא דלא כרב הונא. ובפירוש דסוגיא דהתם אין להאריך כאן:
Tosafot on Ketubot 57b:9:1.english: The refutation of Rav Huna is a conclusive refutation - [This is] surprising, for here [Rav Huna] stands refuted, whereas in the chapter Na'arah HaMe'orasah (Nedarim 70b), the anonymous Gemara's discussion follows his view, as it says regarding the statement of Rabbi Eliezer — [that case of a grown woman (bogeret) who waited twelve months] which [the Gemara] cited above: "For a bogeret, thirty days is sufficient; say: a bogeret, and [a na'arah] who waited [twelve months]" — and this is in accordance with Rav Huna. And it seems [right] to explain that this is what [the Gemara there] is saying: "For a bogeret, thirty days is sufficient" — [meaning:] how can the Mishnah teach "a bogeret who waited twelve months," which implies that for a bogeret it is never sufficient without twelve months, [when in fact] thirty days is sufficient, such as where he betrothed her after she had [already] waited twelve months in her majority (bagrut)? And [the Gemara] answers: Teach [the Mishnah as] "a bogeret, and [a na'arah] who waited [twelve months]." And now [the Mishnah] teaches an unspecified bogeret both together with a na'arah who waited twelve months and together with a widow who waited thirty days, because there is a bogeret whose law is like a na'arah with twelve months — such as where she reached majority for one day and was betrothed — and there is a bogeret whose law is like a widow — such as where she remained twelve months in her majority and was [then] betrothed; and now [that passage] accords not with Rav Huna. And there is no [need] to elaborate here on the explanation of the passage there.
